$comment: A tree-point file with a point outside the extent its host block publishes is not in the host
frame, and is refused by name rather than placed (HPS-53).
`hosts.unreal.foliage_points` states a path and no frame: no CRS, no linear unit. A fixed-frame
host's origin is metric UTM on every order, while the file beside it is in the delivery CRS, which
on a State Plane foot tier is another grid in another unit. Foot coordinates minus a metre origin
is a number that looks exactly like a position, so a reader that subtracts and places reports
success with every tree a thousand kilometres off site.
Where the format states no frame beside a pointer, HPS-53 permits one substitute, and it is a
comparison of published values: a point outside the extent this host's own block publishes is not
in this frame. The extent here is the landscape's — `heightmap.landscape_transform`, the span the
reader already applies to the Landscape, centred on the georeference origin. With the embedded
`manifest` that is 8 x 126 quads at 141.369... cm east and 138.988... cm north: 712.5 m either side
of the origin's easting and 700.5 m either side of its northing. The two half-spans differ on
purpose, and the just-inside / just-outside rows sit between them, so a reader that swaps the
axes of the extent fails two rows rather than none.
The comparison runs ONE way. A file inside the extent is `parsed`, which is the absence of
evidence against its frame and never a showing of it. A file with ANY point outside is
`unplaceable`: the frame belongs to the file, not to the point, so one point off the landscape
refuses the layer rather than being dropped from it — a reader that keeps the points that happen
to land inside is placing a file it has evidence against.
`unplaceable` is a named SKIP, never a conversion and never a failure of the import: the reader
does not scale feet to metres, does not reproject, keeps none of the rows, says why, and the
terrain, the imagery and the buildings beside the layer import as they would have.
`manifest` is one embedded document every row is read against; `csv` is the payload verbatim.
The foot row's coordinates are the MAGNITUDE a State Plane foot grid states for this AOI, not a
projection of the same trees — nothing here converts them, so nothing depends on their digits.
`parsedRows` is asserted on a `parsed` outcome only; on `unplaceable` the rows are discarded.

rows.name: a file inside the landscape extent is placed as it always was
a State Plane foot file beside a metric UTM origin is unplaceable, not a thousand kilometres away
one point off the landscape refuses the file: the frame belongs to the file, not to the point
712 m east and 700 m north of the origin are inside both half-spans
713 m east is outside the easting half-span of 712.5 m
701 m north is outside the northing half-span of 700.5 m, though inside the easting one
